provenance.text: Real GitHub PR-derived SWE tasks (SWE-bench-style: issue + gold patch + test patch) from Python repos, with LLM-built Docker environments and eval scripts; plus LLM agent trajectories. Pipeline code derived from SWE-Factory; inspired by SWE-rebench.

quotes.quote: OpenSWE is the largest fully transparent framework for SWE agent training in Python, comprising 45,320 executable Docker environments spanning over 12.8k repositories, with all Dockerfiles, evaluation scripts, and infrastructure fully open-sourced for reproducibility.

With $891K spent on environment construction and an additional $576K on trajectory sampling and difficulty-aware curation, the project yields about 13,000 curated trajectories from roughly 9,000 quality-guaranteed environments.

To improve the representativeness of our dataset, we retain only repositories with at least five GitHub stars ... We constrain the dataset to PRs from repositories whose primary programming language is Python ... each PR is required to have at least one associated issue with an issue description ... we require non-empty patches to non-test code
quotes.source_url: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.13023 (Section 3.2 GitHub PR Filtering; NOTE: no license filter and no SWE-bench-repo exclusion among the four stages)

quotes.quote: This infrastructure enables the simultaneous processing of an extensive corpus of approximately 572,114 GitHub PRs ... We use Deepseek-v3.2 as the construction model.

To construct our training data, we used the GLM-4.7 model to sample the trajectory from the entire OpenSWE and SWE-rebench (filtered) datasets four times under the OpenHands or SWE-Agent (temperature 1.0, 200k context, and 300 steps). We then collected all trajectories that were correct in one or two of the four attempts under the same instance. ... We also remove all data that contains 'git pull' in the bash action to avoid reward hacking.

`openswe_oss.jsonl`: We have fully open-sourced all repositories whose licenses allow redistribution, including MIT, Apache, GPL, and BSD licenses. `openswe_other.jsonl`: For repositories that cannot be directly open-sourced, we provide the corresponding Dockerfile and evaluation scripts instead.
OpenSWE is inspired by SWE-Rebench and SWE-Factory. We thank these teams for their open-source contributions.

contamination_notes: HIGH UNCERTAINTY. Neither the card nor the paper states any exclusion of SWE-bench / SWE-bench Verified / Multi-SWE-bench repositories or instances (grep of the paper for exclud*/overlap/contaminat*/dedup*/held-out in relation to SWE-bench returned nothing; the 4 PR filters are stars>=5, Python, linked issue, non-test code change). The GitHub README's own schema example uses `psf/requests` as the example repo name (requests is a SWE-bench test repo). HF discussion #4 cites instance `pandas-dev__pandas-17888` in filtered_ids.csv. With 12.8k Python repos selected by star count, inclusion of the 12 SWE-bench repos (django, sympy, scikit-learn, ...) and even identical PR instances is plausible and NOT ruled out by any statement - UNVERIFIED (data gated). The project reports SWE-bench Verified scores for models trained on it. Separate quality issue (discussion #4, 2026-05-28): "A subset of eval_scripts apply the golden patch before grading — verifiers pass without any agent fix".
